title: Teaching & Learning Strategies
whatItIs: The third marked area, with 8 competences. It asks whether the instructor helps the pupil learn actively, choosing the right technique at the right time.
keyFacts: Coaching extends the range of options; it isn't an automatic replacement for instruction.
Direct instruction helps early-stage pupils with new situations, or a pupil who is clearly struggling.
Technically incorrect information that might lead to a safety-critical situation is an automatic fail.
Good information is accurate, relevant and timely: failing any one makes the others redundant.
Use real situations on the lesson to show when, how and why to use a technique.
Allow enough uninterrupted time to practise new skills.

items.title: Choose the location
items.text: Select a suitable place for the explanation or demonstration.

items.title: Explain the why
items.text: Learning is helped when the learner knows why a skill is needed.

items.title: Check understanding
items.text: Encourage questions; repeat or rephrase until they understand.

items.title: Let them practise
items.text: Give enough practice, then feedback on any obstacles.

b.label: Coaching
points: Engaged pupil finds their own solutions
Pupil analyses and owns the learning

onTheTest.question: When is direct instruction most useful, according to DVSA guidance?
options: Helping an early-stage pupil cope with a new situation
Never: coaching should always be used
Only once the pupil is ready for test
When the pupil is performing well
onTheTest.why: Examiner guidance 3.24: it helps early-stage pupils with new situations, or a pupil clearly struggling.

onTheTest.question: An instructor says only 'you're a bit close to these parked cars'. What's the problem?
options: It's unclear: how close is 'a bit', and does it matter?
It's too detailed for a learner
It should be said only after the lesson
onTheTest.why: Examiner guidance 3.24: it could start coaching on a weakness, but on its own it is unclear and of little use.

traps: Frequent explanations and demonstrations support some learners but can demotivate others.
Focusing on teaching tools instead of learning outcomes shows a lack of competence.
Explaining while you drive is level 3; full 'commentary driving' is a level 4 competence.
